text:
Jiri Kulich's season has been about getting back on the ice and then staying there. The Sabres' 2022 first-rounder (28th overall) was cleared after a concussion on Nov. 4, has played two games since, and by Nov. 10 Buffalo Hockey Beat was writing that he could be a healthy scratch. Lindy Ruff, as Bleacher Report's Joe Yerdon relayed it, believes Kulich is still trying to find his game and that it's in there, after a handful of injury setbacks this year.

The numbers back the coach's patience more than the box score does. Three points in ten games and one goal on 1.97 expected, but Buffalo has taken 56% of the expected goals with him on the ice at five on five, well above the team without him, and the on-ice goals have lagged. He scored 18 goals in his first 75 NHL games, and that finishing is the reason he's here. The minutes are the issue: down three and a half a night, to about 13. Our range on him is wide (12 goals as a middle guess). What to watch is simple: whether he's dressed.
